operator_io_quirks: All identifiers lowercase, no spaces/mixed case; quoting still required by spec but no escaping stress here.
ship_date declared TEXT (not DATE) -> dispatches to String fuzzer, not Date; text-stored dates format 'YYYY-MM-DD' (e.g. 2016-01-08).
zip (customer) and area (city) declared REAL but hold integer-ish values (33415.0, 1.3); storage real.
zip_code (driver) declared INTEGER, storage integer, 5-digit; model_year INTEGER 2005-2009.
customer.cust_id values are sparse (193,304,314,381,493), not 1..N; shipment.cust_id references them.
shipment has 4 FKs to 4 distinct parents (customer, city, driver, truck); all parents exist and are unique PKs.
driver.city/state are constant (Memphis/TN, distinct=1); truck.make distinct=3; customer.cust_type distinct=3.
No NOT NULL constraints anywhere (notnull=0 all columns); no CHECK/UNIQUE declared besides PKs.
No composite keys, no self-references, no dangling FKs in this DB.
Small tables: driver=11, truck=12, customer=100, city=601, shipment=960; no huge-table sampling needed.
shipment.weight REAL with wide range (3528..17154), 692 distinct.
phone/address/cust_name are free text with punctuation ('(', ')', '-', '&', ',', apostrophes in Pard's).
operator_ts_expectations: ship_date -> String fuzzer (declared TEXT): random a-zA-Z0-9() strings, NOT dates; kills date-comparison queries (FN/FP).
cust_type/make/state/city -> String fuzzer: random strings, not the 3/49/33-value enums; breaks equality/IN filters.
zip/area REAL -> Number(scale=4) floats in [-10^4,10^4]; plausible-ish but not 5-digit zips or small areas.
population/annual_revenue INTEGER -> Number(scale=4) in [-10^4,10^4]; annual_revenue real values are ~10^7-10^8, so TS values implausible (FN on revenue thresholds).
model_year INTEGER -> Number(scale=4) in [-10^4,10^4]; years 2005-2009 plausible but random.
PKs (city_id, cust_id, ship_id, ...) -> Number with max_l0=inf, fresh draws; sparse original cust_id not reproduced.
FK columns (shipment.cust_id etc.) drawn from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement -> duplicates and ties present, good for join/group-by.
String fuzzer contaminate (suffix/prefix/drop char) makes phone/address/cust_name noisy; LIKE '%...%' queries may still match by chance.
No NOT NULL/CHECK -> rows rarely fail insert; TS keeps most rows, so cardinality close to chosen size.
driver.city constant 'Memphis' in original; TS String fuzzer will produce varied strings -> loses the constant-column signal (FP on city='Memphis').
Number list-range quirk (upper end overwritten to full range) widens value spread beyond observed min/max.
Small parent tables (driver=11, truck=12) with TS sizes up to 2500 -> FK fan-out much larger than original, changes join cardinalities.
